basics.name: Cian McCaul
basics.label: Computer Science student at DCU
basics.headline: I build software that runs real businesses.
basics.summary: I built the booking, payments and staff platform that **BodyMed Healthcare**, a clinic in Clontarf, runs on. Patients book and pay online, and staff run the clinic from one hub.
bio: I’m Cian and I live in Dublin. I spent my early years in Fall River, Nova Scotia, before my family moved to Clontarf in 2015. Starting again in a new country taught me to adapt quickly, and I still like being thrown into something new.
What I enjoy most is working with businesses and making their day easier. At BodyMed I’ve gone from admin work to building the systems the clinic runs on.
On Saturday mornings I’m head coach at Rugbytots, running four classes for young children. My favourite moment is a child finally scoring their first conversion.

projects.name: Clinic platform
projects.tagline: Online booking, payments and a staff hub for a real clinic.
projects.description: Patients could only book by phone or email, late cancellations and no-shows cost therapists money, and reception tracked payments by hand. I built one system on top of the clinic’s diary (Cliniko) and payments (Stripe). Patients book and pay in a couple of minutes, reception handles refunds, fees and phone bookings from one dashboard, and each therapist is paid straight into their own Stripe account.
projects.outcome: TODO: one measured result, for example the share of bookings now made online.
projects.fact: Live at book.bodymed.ie since October 2026, taking real bookings and payments every day.
highlights: Built online booking, payments and a staff hub on top of the clinic’s diary (Cliniko) and Stripe Connect. Live since October 2026, taking real bookings and payments every day.
Designed a pay-then-book flow with slot holds, idempotent webhooks and automatic refunds, so a patient is never left paid but not booked, or booked twice.
Wrote a failure modes and effects analysis, a test plan, a runbook and architecture decision records before launch.

projects.name: AI email triage
projects.tagline: Sorts the clinic inbox, drafts replies and learns from staff edits.
projects.description: Sorts clinic email by topic and urgency, drafts replies from the clinic’s own handbook, and learns from the changes staff make before they press send. A red-flag check runs on every email and overrules the AI when a symptom needs a doctor.
projects.outcome: TODO: one measured result, for example how often the sorter agrees with staff.
projects.fact: 37 tests, including one that checks every sample email lands in its expected folder.
highlights: Built an inbox assistant that sorts clinic email into four folders, drafts replies from the clinic’s handbook and learns from the edits staff make.
Added a red-flag safety check that overrules the AI when a symptom needs a doctor, a rules fallback and 37 tests.
projects.imageAlt: An email in the triage demo titled Pins and needles getting worse. One panel explains why it was sorted into Priority, and a safety check says the draft reply tells the patient to contact their GP or emergency department first.

projects.name: Clinic chatbot
projects.tagline: Answers common questions and points patients to the right physio.
projects.description: A chat widget for a physio clinic. It answers common questions, suggests the right physio for back, knee, shoulder or sports injuries, and hands anything else to staff. The replies are plain rules, not AI, so the clinic decides exactly what patients are told.
projects.fact: Rule-based on purpose: every answer is predictable, so nothing goes off-script on health advice.
projects.imageAlt: The chatbot demo on a fictional clinic’s site. Asked about a back injury, it suggests a physiotherapist and offers a link to book.

projects.name: Jarvis site monitor
projects.tagline: Explains outages in plain English and proposes guarded fixes.
projects.description: Checks the sites I look after every 15 minutes. When one goes down it explains the outage in plain English with AI and, if the fix is small and safe, opens a pull request I can approve from my phone.
projects.outcome: TODO: one measured result, for example outages caught before a customer reported them.
projects.fact: Every AI-proposed fix passes five guard rails enforced in code, not in a prompt.
highlights: Built a monitor that checks sites every 15 minutes, explains outages with an LLM and opens small fix pull requests.
Enforced five guard rails in code: pull request only, one file, under 15 changed lines, scoped token, fail closed.

guardRails.title: Never touches main
guardRails.detail: It only ever opens a pull request.

guardRails.title: One file only
guardRails.detail: A fix that touches more is rejected.

guardRails.title: Under 15 changed lines
guardRails.detail: Anything bigger is flagged for manual review.

guardRails.title: Scoped token
guardRails.detail: Access to the monitored sites’ repos only. It can’t modify itself.

guardRails.title: Fails closed
guardRails.detail: If anything is ambiguous: no pull request, just a note in the email.
